_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); automaker signals, the early era

pit_profile.why: Ford Motor Company: 'We are one of the world’s largest producers of cars and trucks combined.' ('Our vehicle brands include Ford, Mercury, Lincoln, and Volvo; our Jaguar and Land Rover brands are held for sale as of the fourth quarter of 2007.'); among its risk factors, 'A significant decline in industry sales, particularly in the United States or Europe, resulting from slowing economic growth, geo-political events or other factors.' and 'An increase in or acceleration of market shift away from sales of trucks, sport utility vehicles, or other more profitable vehicles in the United States.'; 'The automotive industry is also a highly competitive, cyclical business that has a wide and growing variety of product offerings from a growing number of manufacturers.' (the industry, not the company's own earnings, is called cyclical: DURABLE, the AVGO precedent) (its own FY2007 10-K); no disruption theme in the registry is live for an automaker on this date, so the watch list is empty and the 10-K's words on the shift away from trucks and SUVs stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

(the industry, not the company's own earnings, is called cyclical: DURABLE, the AVGO precedent) (its own FY2007 10-K); no disruption theme in the registry is live for an automaker on this date, so the watch list is empty and the 10-K's words on the shift away from trucks and SUVs stay here (the PEP obesity rule). durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.11x; -55% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.73; conservative 2yr +194%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -52.6%/yr (worst year FY02-FY05, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-23.5%/yr (Q3 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 6.9-yr ex-FY06 ex-FY07 median

BULL.desc: EPS +21.3%/yr (FY02-FY05 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +94.1%/yr (best 2-yr run FY02-FY05); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: F (retrospective, 2008-12-05) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.11x (63.2% downside to Bear $1 / +561.8% upside to Bull $18) | Adj composite 1.95 vs market 1.22: gap +0.73 [UNDERVALUED] | -55% above the EPP floor $6 (6x FY08E $1.00) | Conservative 2-yr case: +194.1% total (+97.1%/yr) | At 2.7x FY08E the 15% hurdle price $4 sits at or below the BASE case; wholesale units -21.0% in Q3 2008, forward revenues -21.9% (no Q4 2008 revenue guide, Q3 2008 revenue as reported); no disruption theme is live for an automaker on this date.
